name: Water fasting
lead: Water fasting, also called extended or zero-calorie fasting, is abstaining from all food and caloric drinks for 24 hours or more, usually several days. In looksmaxxing communities it is used for rapid fat loss and with claims about skin and facial leanness.[1][2]

Physiology sources report that early weight loss in a prolonged fast includes a large share of lean tissue, and that the body later shifts toward ketosis.[1] Documented risks include electrolyte disturbances, gallstones and refeeding syndrome.[1]
infobox: More than 24 hours; often 3 days or longer

paras: Metabolic changes begin about 3 to 5 hours after eating. Early in a prolonged fast gluconeogenesis is high and roughly two-thirds of early weight lost is lean muscle; later ketones replace glucose as the main fuel for the nervous system, and the fat-to-lean loss ratio is about 7:6.[1] Weight loss averages about 0.9 kg per day in week one and 0.3 kg per day by week three.[1] Sodium, potassium and magnesium fall significantly, which can cause hyponatremia.[1]

Fasting is central to many religious traditions, and in the early twentieth century it was promoted by alternative-health writers such as Upton Sinclair, whose 1911 book The Fasting Cure made sweeping claims.[1] Linda Hazzard's strict regimens caused many patient deaths.[1] Angus Barbieri fasted for 382 days in 1965 and 1966 under medical observation.[1]

A looksmax.org guide describes the author fasting for about two years, now three days monthly, with a disclaimer that it is not medical advice.[3] Other users ask whether to choose water fasting or one meal a day, with replies about low-carbohydrate approaches.[4] A user reports a three-week fast with breaks in which fat loss was large but hair fell out heavily afterward and later regrew.[3] Another thread discusses prolonged fasts with a reply advising basics and time for skin and collagen.[5]

Refeeding syndrome, a shift in potassium, magnesium and phosphate after reintroducing food, can be fatal and can occur after about 4 to 5 days without food.[1] Fasting can raise gallstone risk.[1] Intermittent fasting sources report that fasting is not recommended in pregnancy, children, older adults or people prone to eating disorders.[2]

Alternate-day fasting improved cardiometabolic markers in overweight adults in studies cited in encyclopedic sources, and a 2021 review found moderate alternate-day fasting for 2 to 6 months lowered body weight and BMI.[1][2] A 2018 pilot of 8-hour time-restricted feeding in 23 obese adults reported weight loss.[6] These studies concern shorter or intermittent fasts. No studies found on repeated multi-day water fasts for facial appearance.

timeline.event: Upton Sinclair publishes The Fasting Cure.[1]
Angus Barbieri begins a supervised 382-day fast.[1]

lore.intro: Water fasting is discussed on looksmax.org as a fast fat-loss and skin tool, with some users reporting side effects such as hair shedding.[3]

claims.claim: Water fasting strips fat faster than eating less
claims.believers: Users weighing it against OMAD say they are willing to fast for faster results, and a guide author reports regular monthly fasts.[3][4]
claims.experts: Physiology sources report that early weight lost in a prolonged fast is largely lean tissue, with fat and lean loss roughly 7:6 later on.[1]

claims.believers: One user reports heavy shedding after a three-week fast with weekly breaks, with regrowth later.[3]
claims.experts: No published studies found in the sources reviewed on water fasting and hair loss; electrolyte and nutrient changes in prolonged fasts are documented.[1]

card.summary: Multi-day zero-calorie fasting for fast fat loss; documented risks include refeeding syndrome and loss of lean tissue.
card.note: Refeeding syndrome can be fatal and can occur after about 4 to 5 days without food.

quick.overview:
Water fasting means no calories for a day or more. Forum users use it for rapid fat loss and say it improves skin, and some report hair shedding afterward.

Physiology sources report a large share of early weight loss is lean tissue, and studies cover shorter intermittent fasts rather than repeated extended ones.
quick.mechanism: With no intake, the body uses glycogen and then protein and fat, shifting toward ketone use for the brain over days.
quick.risks: Documented risks include electrolyte loss, gallstones and refeeding syndrome, which can be fatal. Fasting is not recommended for pregnancy, children, older adults or people prone to eating disorders.
